title: Design Patterns in Ruby — Quick Revision

sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Design pattern questions in Ruby interviews are really about recognising when a Rails app's models are doing too much and knowing which pattern extracts the right responsibility. Service objects extract business logic from fat models (SRP). Form objects handle multi-model forms or complex validation scenarios. Query objects encapsulate complex ActiveRecord query logic. Value objects represent domain values with equality semantics (Money, EmailAddress). Decorators extend objects without subclassing. This page covers SOLID applied to Ruby (with the insight that in Ruby, Strategy is just passing a Proc), the five patterns Rails engineers reach for most, SimpleDelegator as a lightweight decorator, and the decision between a service object and a concern — the answer depends on whether the logic is shared and whether it involves external I/O.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: solid-in-ruby, service-objects, value-objects, structural-patterns, behavioral-patterns. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
